data.title: Dan Ives Sees Major New Chapter for Popular Meme Stock
data.description:
GameStop may still be in the early stages of a much larger transformation, according to Yorkville Ives, which sees the retailer evolving into a leaner and more profitable collectibles platform.

Analyst Dan Ives reiterated an Outperform rating on GameStop with a $32 price target, arguing that 2027 could become an important inflection year.

The biggest change is happening in the company's sales mix.

Ives said collectibles are now approaching half of GameStop's revenue, giving the company a much different profile than the legacy video-game retailer investors once knew.

The key advantage, in his view, is infrastructure.

GameStop already has a nationwide store footprint, a long-standing trade-in culture, and a customer base accustomed to buying, selling and swapping products.

Its relationship with PSA adds another layer.

Participating GameStop stores can act as intake points for card grading and authentication, allowing collectors to access services that would otherwise typically require mailing items directly.

In effect, GameStop's stores are becoming a distributed intake and authentication network for a broader collectibles ecosystem, Ives wrote.

The analyst also highlighted GameStop's digital power packs business, arguing that the real opportunity may come from the transactions and higher-margin activity that follow the initial sale.

Investor Takeaway

I think the most interesting part of Ives' thesis is that he is not betting on GameStop simply becoming a better video-game retailer.

He is arguing that the company is building a collectibles infrastructure network.

That distinction matters because authentication, grading, trade-ins and resale can potentially create repeat activity and higher-margin economics around each customer relationship.

Ives also sees strategic value in GameStop's eBay stake.

He believes there is logic in combining eBay's marketplace liquidity with GameStop's physical stores, authentication capabilities and trade-in infrastructure, whether through an eventual acquisition or commercial partnership.

For investors, the key things to watch are collectibles mix, PSA transaction growth, margins, eBay-related developments and whether 2027 delivers the operating inflection Ives expects.

GameStop shares reached a new 52-week high of $28.30 Thursday, suggesting investors are increasingly willing to give the transformation thesis another look.

data.title: Bank of America Makes Massive Call on CarMax Stock
data.description:
CarMax is getting a major Wall Street vote of confidence after Bank of America upgraded the used-car retailer to Buy from Underperform and raised its price target to $65 from $50.

The new target implies roughly 25% to 30% upside from where shares were trading around the time of the call. CarMax stock rose more than 3% in premarket trading Thursday following the upgrade.

The bullish turn centers on something surprisingly simple: price transparency.

Bank of America analysts Alexander Perry and Jack Joyce said CarMax has become the most price-competitive it has been in years as tighter Federal Trade Commission enforcement forces rival used-car dealers to advertise more complete, all-in vehicle prices rather than relying on lower headline prices that exclude certain fees.

That matters because CarMax has long operated with relatively transparent pricing.

As competitors are pushed toward similar disclosure standards, BofA believes some of CarMax's apparent pricing disadvantage is disappearing.

The operating numbers are already encouraging.

CarMax's comparable used-vehicle sales increased roughly 13% in its fiscal second quarter, while the broader industry declined about 2%, according to the analysts. BofA believes the gap reflects both improved relative pricing and stronger customer perception.

The bank also sees a longer runway for gains as more dealers comply with the new pricing environment and consumers become increasingly focused on the full cost of buying a used vehicle.

Investor Takeaway

I think the most interesting part of BofA's upgrade is that it is not relying on a dramatic rebound in the used-car market.

It is arguing that the rules of competition are becoming more favorable for CarMax.

If competing dealers can no longer make vehicles appear cheaper by leaving fees out of advertised prices, CarMax's longstanding no-haggle and transparent-pricing model becomes easier for consumers to compare directly.

That could support market-share gains even if the overall used-car backdrop remains challenging.

For investors, the key things to watch are comparable used-unit sales, gross profit per vehicle, market-share trends and whether the FTC-driven pricing advantage persists beyond the initial compliance period.

CarMax will also host a strategic update on Nov. 3, giving investors another opportunity to see whether management believes the recent sales momentum can translate into durable earnings growth.

The Loan does not bear interest and is repayable on demand. No bonus was paid or is payable by the Company in connection with the Loan. The Company intends to use the proceeds for general working capital and corporate purposes and intends to repay the Loan from future capital raises or general revenue.

data.title: U.S. Stocks Fall as Credit Fears Haunt Tech Sector — Update
data.description:
By Rob Curran

U.S. stocks fell as fears mounted that artificial-intelligence profits would not come soon enough to meet increasingly expensive credit obligations for CoreWeave and other aspiring hyperscalers.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 175.28 points, or 0.34%, to 52002.41. The S&P 500 lost 84.62 points, or 1.09%, to 7659.44. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 572.99 points, or 2.14%, to 26140.03. The tech-heavy index lost about 4.5% for the week, its biggest decline since the week ended June 26.

Shares of CoreWeave fell 12% and are down more than 50% from their highs earlier this year as concerns about the cloud-computing company's ability to pay down debt lingered.

"Inevitably, with the cost of credit and capital rising to unaffordable levels, plans will have to be scaled back and capex reduced sooner or later," said Lorenzo Di Mattia, founder and chief investment officer at hedge-fund firm Sibilla Capital. Di Mattia has a modest short position on the U.S. stock market, he said.

Speaking at an International Monetary Fund event in Bangkok, Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh declined to give any rate guidance ahead of the October meeting of the central bank's rate-setting committee. Rising oil prices and broader inflation worries spurred long-term Treasury yields higher.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury note rose 0.011 percentage point to 5.097%. The yield on the 30-year bond rose 0.009 percentage point to 5.436%, recouping some losses from Thursday but still registering its biggest weekly drop in more than a year. The yield on the two-year Treasury fell 0.013 percentage point to 4.734%, completing its largest one-week retreat since August.

The Russell 2000 index of small cap stocks sank deeper into correction territory, paring its year-to-date gains to around 10%.

Oil futures rose $3.44 or 3.5%, to $101.41 a barrel in New York after Ukraine renewed attacks on Russian refineries, and the safety of ships in the Strait of Hormuz remained in question. For the week, West Texas Intermediate oil futures rose by 10%, their biggest gain since the week ended July 17, in the wake of a surprisingly large drawdown in U.S. inventories.

Gold futures rose $11.80, or 0.28%, to $4159.50 a troy ounce. The precious metal lost 0.8% of its value this week, with losses limited by an abrupt return to favor at midweek as a traditional safe-haven for investments. In another reversal of 2026 trends, the U.S. dollar lost ground against rivals.

Selling in the chip and technology stocks started Wednesday and was particularly intense in semiconductor-heavy Asian markets. South Korea's Kospi index rebounded modestly Friday but remains more than 37% down from its summer peak after losing 14% of its value this week. That is the index's the biggest weekly loss since the onset of the global financial crisis in October 2008.

The decline in shares of CoreWeave--which has borrowed at least $35 billion to build data centers--came despite a vote of confidence from Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia and one of the company's largest suppliers.

Nvidia shares declined 1.4% to $214.13 and Dell Technologies, another CoreWeave supplier, retreated 4.6% to $451.71. Dell's stock lost more than 22% of its value this week for its biggest five-day loss since it relaunched on public markets in 2018.

"We're in risky territory but what you may see is some M&A in this space," CBOE Global Markets' senior vice president JJ Kinahan said. "That's what often happens when you get this [credit stress.]"

Varonis Systems' shares rose 2.9% to $48.72 after closely held cybersecurity firm Proofpoint agreed to acquire the data-security company for about $6.3 billion, honing its focus on AI security.

Apple, which has moved more cautiously on AI than many rivals, rose 0.4% $343.46. Orders for its iPhone Duo foldable smart phone are off to a strong start.

The financial sector was another bright spot as earnings from regional bank holding companies including M&T Bank and Citizens Financial were generally strong.

Write to Rob Curran at rob.curran@wsj.com

data.title: Actinium Pharmaceuticals Announces Inducement Grants to New Employees
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Actinium Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NYSE American: ATNM) ("Actinium" or the "Company"), a pioneer in the development of targeted radiotherapies, today announced inducement equity awards to Matt David, M.D., the Company's newly appointed Chief Financial Officer, and Sean Maenpaa, the Company's newly appointed Senior Vice President, Business Development.

In connection with Dr. David's appointment, on October 14, 2026 the Company granted Dr. David a non-qualified stock option to purchase 250,000 shares of the Company's common stock at an exercise price of $0.97 per share, equal to the closing price of Actinium's common stock on the NYSE American on October 14, 2026. The option has a ten-year term; 28% of the shares underlying the option vest on the first anniversary of the grant date, and the remainder vest in equal monthly installments of 2% of the shares underlying the option over the following 36 months. Dr. David was also granted 250,000 restricted stock units ("RSUs"), of which 125,000 vest in three equal annual installments on the first, second and third anniversaries of the grant date and 125,000 vest in full on the third anniversary of the grant date, as well as up to 75,000 RSUs that vest upon the achievement of specified corporate milestones.

In connection with Mr. Maenpaa's appointment, on October 12, 2026 the Company granted Mr. Maenpaa a non-qualified stock option to purchase 40,000 shares of the Company's common stock at an exercise price of $1.06 per share, equal to the closing price of Actinium's common stock on the NYSE American on October 12, 2026. The option has a ten-year term; 28% of the shares underlying the option vest on the first anniversary of the grant date, and the remainder vest in equal monthly installments of 2% of the shares underlying the option over the following 36 months. Mr. Maenpaa was also granted 20,000 RSUs that vest in three equal annual installments on the first, second and third anniversaries of the grant date, and 50,000 RSUs that vest on the third anniversary of the grant date, subject to the fulfillment of certain corporate milestones.

Vesting of each award is subject to the executive's continued service with the Company through the applicable vesting date. The awards were granted outside of the Company's Amended and Restated 2019 Stock Plan as an inducement material to each executive's entering into employment with the Company in accordance with Section 711(a) of the NYSE American Company Guide, and are subject to the terms of the Actinium Pharmaceuticals, Inc. 2026 Employment Inducement Award Plan and the applicable award agreements.

About Actinium Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

Actinium is a pioneer in targeted radiotherapies designed to improve outcomes for patients with cancer. The company employs a biology-driven approach to develop differentiated radiopharmaceuticals for solid tumors and hematologic malignancies. Its mission is to transform cancer treatment through innovative radioconjugates that maximize therapeutic efficacy while minimizing toxicity to healthy tissue by combining expertise in tumor biology, translational medicine, and radiochemistry. Since inception, Actinium has focused on developing innovative radiotherapies. Its pipeline reflects this strategy across three areas: (1) solid tumor therapeutics including ATNM-400 and Actimab-A with pan-tumor potential; (2) Actimab-A as a therapeutic backbone for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) in collaboration with the National Cancer Institute (NCI); and (3) targeted conditioning agents including Iomab-B for bone marrow transplant and Iomab-ACT for cell and gene therapy conditioning. ATNM-400 targets a novel antigen distinct from PSMA and has demonstrated preclinical activity across metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and breast cancer, and is being evaluated in a first-in-human Phase 1 study in mCRPC. Actimab-A has shown improved survival in relapsed/refractory AML with CLAG-M and is advancing toward a Phase 2/3 trial, with additional development ongoing through a CRADA with the NCI. Actinium is also advancing preclinical solid tumor programs and holds ~250 patents and patent applications, including intellectual property related to cyclotron-based production of Ac-225. For more information, please visit www.actiniumpharma.com.

data.title: Wall Street Just Put $1,000 on Meta
data.description:
Meta Platforms Inc. (META, Financials), the social-media and AI startup, recently got one of Wall Street's most aggressive targets.

Truist up its price target to a Street-high $1,000 from $763 and maintained a Buy rating in advance of third-quarter earnings.

The call showed increasing confidence that Meta's AI spending is beginning to show up in the business.

Meta's Muse AI agent has had great monetization, user engagement and adoption, noted Truist analyst Youssef Squali.

He is predicting third-quarter sales of around $63.9 billion, at the high end of Meta's guidance range of $61 billion to $64 billion. This is the opportunity.

The issue is that Meta is pouring money into building the infrastructure underlying those goods, so bigger expectations now call for clearer returns.

Truist's greater long-term predictions also accounted for increased capital investment, which also included Muse. That trade-off is becoming a key part of the Meta tale.

Investors are no longer questioning if Meta will invest much on AI. They're asking how fast such investments can create new income and grow the existing advertising company.

The next catalyst comes on Oct. 21, when results should demonstrate whether the confidence underlying the $1,000 goal is justified.

data.title: Abakkus Flexi Cap Fund September portfolio: 35 stocks, including Groww and NTPC, see higher holdings
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 16 -- Sunil Singhania-backed Abakkus Flexi Cap Fund increased its holdings in Groww, NTPC and HDFC Bank in September, while adding pharmaceutical company Zydus Lifesciences to its portfolio and exiting Cyient DLM. The fund raised its holdings in 35 existing stocks and trimmed two others during the month.

The fund's September portfolio disclosure shows changes across existing investments rather than a broad reshuffle. Its portfolio contained 46 stocks at the end of September, unchanged from August.

Groww parent Billionbrains Garage Ventures was among the fund's biggest additions by share quantity. Abakkus Flexi Cap Fund increased its holding by 30 lakh shares, taking it to 90 lakh shares in September.

The fund also added 13.5 lakh shares of NTPC, taking its holding to 78.5 lakh shares, and bought another 4 lakh shares of HDFC Bank, raising its total to 50 lakh shares.

Reliance Industries was another stock where the fund increased its exposure. It added 1.25 lakh shares, taking its holding to 19.25 lakh shares. The fund also raised its positions in State Bank of India and ICICI Bank.

The fund added Zydus Lifesciences as a new position, buying 7 lakh shares during September. The holding was valued at around Rs.81.34 crore at the end of the month.

At the other end, the fund sold its entire holding in Cyient DLM, exiting the stock after holding 1.51 lakh shares in August. The position was worth around Rs.12.74 crore at the end of that month.

The fund also reduced its holdings in two stocks. It sold 61,807 shares of Divi's Laboratories, bringing its holding down to 1.70 lakh shares. In Oracle Financial Services Software, it sold 45,426 shares, leaving it with around 1.20 lakh shares.

Despite the changes in individual stocks, the fund's portfolio remained spread across 22 sectors. Banking was its largest sector exposure, accounting for around 15.79% of net assets, followed by finance at 10.13%.

The portfolio included a mix of financial services companies, industrial businesses, power producers, technology-related stocks and consumer-facing businesses. Its holdings in banks included HDFC Bank, State Bank of India and ICICI Bank, while its other investments included NTPC and Reliance Industries.

The fund's AUM rose to Rs.7,843.87 crore as of 30 September, from Rs.7,394.97 crore at the end of August. It's cash and cash-equivalent allocation declined slightly to 6.29% of net assets in September, from 6.49% in August.

data.title: Novartis Scraps Another Drug Study. Why the Stock Is Holding Steady. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Mackenzie Tatananni

Novartis has scrapped another clinical trial, adding to a steady stream of clinical setbacks that has left analysts questioning the drugmaker's long-term growth story.

The drugmaker terminated a mid-stage study for Fabhalta in patients with lupus nephritis, a serious kidney-disease complication occurring when the immune system attacks healthy tissue. Researchers were evaluating the drug's efficacy when added to standard treatment.

A clinical database reviewed by Barron's shows Novartis concluded the study after completing its first phase, enrolling just 81 patients out of an originally planned 240. Novartis has also removed mention of the study from its website, where the original link now leads to an error page.

The Swiss drugmaker did not elaborate on the termination, listing only "strategic considerations" in the database entry. This phrasing typically suggests a shift in pipeline priorities or resource allocation rather than underlying safety or efficacy issues.

That distinction may explain why the drugmaker's American depositary receipts barely reacted to the news. In fact, Novartis ticked up 0.2% to $150.62 on Friday, outperforming the broader market on a day when all three major indexes traded solidly in the red.

Another factor: Fabhalta is already on the market with multiple approved indications. In 2023, the Food and Drug Administration first approved the drug to treat a rare blood disorder called PNH, and it has since gained approval for two distinct kidney diseases.

Analysts also held modest expectations for the broader kidney-disease portfolio. Jefferies analyst Michael Leuchten expressed skepticism toward the franchise as recently as July, singling out Fabhalta and pipeline candidate zigakibart as two reasons for caution.

Still, the termination adds to a growing list of clinical setbacks for Novartis. Last month, the company disclosed that a trial for del-desiran, the centerpiece of a recent acquisition, failed to meet its primary goal in patients with a rare neuromuscular disease.

That announcement came just a week after Novartis revealed that pelacarsen failed to significantly reduce the risk of heart attacks and strokes compared with a placebo in a late-stage study. Earlier in September, the company also halted select trials for an experimental cell therapy following three patient deaths linked to a rare autoimmune reaction.

While the Fabhalta study cancellation may not affect shares immediately, it further clouds the narrative around the drugmaker's long-term growth.

That uncertainty is reflected in Wall Street's split consensus: among 10 firms covering Novartis stock, four rate it a Buy or the equivalent, four are sidelined, and two hold a Sell rating.

It's easy to see why analysts are so divided. Goldman Sachs, one of the most prominent bears, expects a looming wave of patent expirations affecting several key drugs — what company executives themselves have dubbed the "largest patent expiry" in Novartis's history — to weigh heavily on earnings momentum.

As Goldman views it, Novartis is entering "a high-risk period of binary catalysts for which the risk is not adequately reflected," particularly given that the stock trades at a premium to its sector peers. For now, analysts are keeping their Sell rating firmly in place.

Write to Mackenzie Tatananni at mackenzie.tatananni@barrons.com

data.title: Live Nation Prices $730M/€600M 2032 Notes and Extends Credit Facilities to 2031
data.description:
Live Nation announced two financing actions to strengthen liquidity and refinance near-term debt. The company completed a private offering of $730.0 million and €600.0 million senior notes due 2032, with proceeds earmarked to redeem its 6.500% Senior Secured Notes due 2027 and for general purposes. Cross-currency swaps on the dollar notes reduce the weighted average interest rate on the new notes to about 5.89% through Oct. 15, 2031. Separately, Live Nation amended its senior secured credit facilities, extending revolver and delayed draw term loan maturities to Oct. 21, 2031 and increasing total commitments to approximately $2.61 billion, enhancing financial flexibility.

data.title: Apple's Next Legal Risk Could Reach $40 Billion
data.description:
Apple Inc. (AAPL, Financials), the creator of the iPhone, is headed for a jury trial in a biometric privacy issue that might become one of its biggest legal concerns.

A federal court in Illinois decided to dismiss most accusations that Apple's Photos app collects and saves facial faceprints without sufficient notice or consent.

The plaintiffs believe that nearly 8 million Illinois citizens are in the certified class.

Penalties can be as high as $5,000 per person for breaches of the state's biometric privacy statute that are willful or negligent. This might result in a possible exposure of up to $40 billion.

That doesn't imply Apple will end up paying anywhere close to that amount.

The corporation disputes any wrongdoing, saying its facial-recognition technology does not make the type of regulated biometric scan that the law covers.

But the potential enormity of the liability makes it a hard case to dismiss.

That matters beyond Apple too. Such arguments over face data might spill over from the internet giant to other big tech corporations as courts figure out how decades-old privacy regulations relate to modern AI-driven recognition techniques.

The crucial question for investors is whether the case remains small or sets a larger precedent. The next step is a jury trial this spring and if Apple will be able to limit the claims before then.`

data.title: Peabody evacuates workers at Wyoming mine after MSHA danger order
data.description:
Peabody Energy's Powder River Mining unit said no miners were injured after workers were evacuated from part of its North Antelope Rochelle mine in Wyoming following an MSHA imminent danger order.

Here are more details:

  • The order, issued on July 9, stemmed from concerns that loose material could fall from a highwall onto an active haul road used by mine vehicles

  • The hazard involved material that could spill over a protective berm and fall onto a roadway used by haul trucks and other vehicles, the company said in a filing

  • The company said mine personnel took measures to mitigate the hazard.

  • MSHA terminated the Section 107(a) order later the same day, according to the company

data.title: NioCorp Provides Preliminary Unaudited Financial Results for the Three-Month Period Ended September 30, 2026
data.description:
CENTENNIAL, CO / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / NioCorp Developments Ltd. ("NioCorp," "our," or the "Company") today provided its preliminary unaudited financial results for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, which are presented below.

The Company reported net income attributable to NioCorp of $3.7 million, or $0.03 per share (basic), for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, as compared to a net loss attributable to NioCorp of $42.7 million, or $0.53 per share (basic), for the three months ended September 30, 2025. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had a cash balance of $405.1 million on its consolidated balance sheet.

The net income for the three months ended September 30, 2026, primarily reflects non-cash gains of approximately $8.5 million related to earnout shares and warrants classified as liabilities on the consolidated balance sheet, driven by a decrease in the closing price of the Company's common shares between June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2026. By contrast, the net loss for the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily reflects non-cash losses of approximately $32.1 million related to earnout shares and warrants classified as liabilities on the consolidated balance sheet, driven by an increase in the closing price of the Company's common shares between June 30, 2025 and September 30, 2025.

The Company continues as a development-stage company, and its operating cash outflows for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, totaled $6.1 million, primarily representing recurring general and administrative costs as well as costs related to the finalization and issuance of the technical and economic study related to the Elk Creek Critical Minerals Project (the "Elk Creek Project"). In addition, its investing outflows for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, totaled $5.9 million, primarily representing additional expenditures associated with ongoing construction of the mine portal at the Elk Creek Project.

NioCorp intends to file its unaudited interim condensed consolidated financial statements for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, in its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q on or before November 16, 2026.

All figures reported above with respect to the three- month period ended September 30, 2026, are preliminary and are unaudited and subject to change and adjustment as the Company prepares its unaudited interim condensed consolidated financial statements for the three- month period ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. Accordingly, investors are cautioned not to place undue reliance on the foregoing information. The Company does not intend to provide preliminary results on a regular basis in the future. The preliminary results provided in this news release constitute "forward-looking information" and "forward-looking statements" within the meaning of applicable Canadian and U.S. securities laws, are based on several assumptions and are subject to a number of risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially. See "Forward-looking Statements."

# # #

NioCorp is developing the Elk Creek Project that is expected to produce niobium, scandium, titanium and several rare earth products, including neodymium-praseodymium oxide, dysprosium oxide, terbium oxide, samarium-europium-gadolinium ("SEG") carbonate, and heavy rare earth carbonate. Niobium is used to produce specialty alloys as well as High Strength, Low Alloy steel, which is a lighter, stronger steel used in automotive, structural, and pipeline applications. Scandium is a specialty metal that can be combined with Aluminum to make alloys with increased strength and improved corrosion resistance. Scandium is also a critical component of advanced solid oxide fuel cells. Titanium is used in various lightweight alloys and is a key component of pigments used in paper, paint and plastics and is also used for aerospace applications, armor, and medical implants. Magnetic rare earths, such as neodymium, praseodymium, terbium, and dysprosium are critical to the making of neodymium-iron-boron magnets, which are used across a wide variety of defense and civilian applications.

data.title: Moody's Upgrades Egypt Ratings, Citing Declining Government Debt
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Moody's Ratings upgraded Egypt's long-term unsecured and issuer ratings, citing the country's fiscal consolidation and reforms to reduce government debt.

The ratings agency gave long-term local and foreign-currency issuer ratings and foreign-currency senior unsecured ratings a B3 rating, up from Caa1. Moody's also gave provisional B3 ratings to the government's senior unsecured medium-term note program, as well as the unsecured MTN program of a government-owned special-purpose vehicle.

Moody's said Egypt's shift to a flexible exchange rate and tighter monetary policy has boosted the economy's resilience, and that the government has strengthened revenue collection while showing expenditure restraint.

"The government's ability to sustain this credit-positive trend despite a challenging external environment and higher oil prices highlights the durability of the improvement, rooted in increased policy effectiveness," Moody's said Friday.

Moody's also maintained a positive outlook, citing declining debt and interest burdens.

Egypt's government debt has fallen from 95.2% of gross domestic product in June 2023 to 81.8% this past June, with debt affordability also beginning to improve, Moody's said.

Write to Elias Schisgall at elias.schisgall@wsj.com
